# Project Details

AGRF taxonomic assignment used multiple databases of different currency. Has resulted in 
many incorrect lineages due to older databases, use of synonyms, or multiplication of names appended at different taxonomic levels with alpha codes to indicate the databases used for naming assignment. 

Taxonomic lineages will be fixed to reflect current names/lineages using the List of Prokaryotic names with Standing in Nomenclature (LPSN) database.  
  - Synonyms will be replaced with the correct names, if no correct name assigned, either pro-correct or preferred name will be used.   
  - Where taxonomic level classification has not been officially allocated yet, a flag will indicate the level has no official assignment.  
  - Where a temporary name, often an alphanumeric code, is used, that temporary name will have the last classified level as a prefix
  - Where lower levels were not able to be assigned to a sequence, the last classified level will be copied across to fill lineage

An API function in R was created to query the database. Where the API was not able to identify the correct name, manual curation will be used.

### Remove underscores and orphaned 1 and 2 letter codes

LPSN does not contain place holder names (numbers and letters). Need to clean up the taxa names that are only made up of letters and remove suffixes added by AGRF.

Any taxa names with numbers will need manual curation, so these are ignored.

```{r}

colnames(df_clean)
# 


# the number of rows should remain the same
nrow(df_clean)
# 


## remove underscores and remove single and double orphaned letters

df_trimmed <- df_clean |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
    c(Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species),
    ~ ifelse(
      stringr::str_detect(.x, "^[^0-9]+$"),  # TRUE only if NO numbers anywhere
      .x |>
        stringr::str_replace_all("_", " ") |>
        stringr::str_remove_all("\\b[A-Za-z]{1,2}\\b") |>
        stringr::str_squish(),
      .x  # leave untouched if ANY number is present
    )
  ))

nrow(df_trimmed)
# 

head(df_trimmed)



## remove any single string in species column
## removes things like species name of soil or bacterium
df_trimmed$Species <- (function(x) {
  x <- base::trimws(base::as.character(x))
  counts <- base::lengths(base::strsplit(x, "\\s+"))
  base::is.na(x) <- (counts < 2)
  base::return(x)
  })(df_trimmed$Species)

nrow(df_trimmed)
# 





## remove orphaned characters
# Exiguobacterium A sp001275385, becomes Exiguobacterium sp001275385
# Ensifer A adhaerens A, becomes Ensifer adhaerens

# df_trimmed$Species <- df_trimmed$Species |>
#   (\(s) {
#     # 1. Replace " UpperCase " with a single space
#     # Matches: space, any single uppercase letter, space
#     s <- base::gsub(" [A-Z] ", " ", s)
#     
#     # 2. Remove trailing " UpperCase"
#     # Matches: space, uppercase letter at the end of the string ($)
#     s <- base::gsub(" [A-Z]$", "", s)
#     
#     base::return(s)
#   })()

# remove single and double letter orphans
# letters are used as database identifiers and are not valid 

df_trimmed$Species <- df_trimmed$Species |> (\(s) {
  #  Remove isolated single or double uppercase letters (e.g., " A " or " AB ")
  # Matches: space, 1 to 2 uppercase letters, followed by a space
  s <- base::gsub(" [A-Z]{1,2} ", " ", s)
  
  # Remove trailing single or double uppercase letters (e.g., " A" or " AB" at end)
  # Matches: space, 1 to 2 uppercase letters, at the end of the string ($)
  s <- base::gsub(" [A-Z]{1,2}$", "", s)
  
  # 3. Clean up any resulting double spaces and trim
  s <- base::gsub("\\s+", " ", s)
  s <- base::trimws(s)
  
  base::return(s)
})()

head(df_trimmed$Species)



nrow(df_trimmed)


df_trimmed |>
  base::subset(base::grepl("^Exiguobacterium", Species)) |> 
  unique()



df_trimmed |>
  base::subset(base::grepl("^Ensifer", Species)) |> 
  unique()



nrow(df_trimmed)
# 


## compare species column data to see what's happened
df_comparison <- base::merge(
  df_clean["Species"], 
  df_trimmed["Species"], 
  by = 0,               # 0 indicates merging by rownames
  suffixes = c("_original", "_trimmed")
) |>
  # Optional: rename the 'Row.names' column back to 'ID' or similar
  (\(d) {
    base::colnames(d)[1] <- "ID"
    base::return(d)
  })()

df_comparison
```

# LSPN API

Register with  the LPSN site and record the login email and password used
https://sso.dsmz.de/auth/realms/DSMZ/login-actions/registration?client_id=api.lpsn&tab_id=4jgxLa3kKA8 

Ensure your .Renviron file contains the fields below to enable login and not record password in the script. Info on modifying .Renviron file: https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/environments/r/managing-r.html 

Format needed for LPSN login:
DSMZ_API_USER = <email>
DSMZ_API_PASSWORD = <password>

## Run API function

Function starts at species level, and searched for genus and species. If it cannot be found it will just search for genus. It works backwards moving up the lineage until the record is found.
At any point when a record is found, it is checked to ensure it is flagged as the  correct name, if it is a synonym, it goes to the correct name and uses that point to move up the lineage. The level where the classification was found is recorded.

Any records not found are logged
Taxa are processed in batches abd the results are saved to a new sheet in a single excelworkbook.

```{r}

# load function
source("LPSN_API_functions.R") 


#Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)

# load combined taxa list
combined_taxa <- readRDS(file = "XXXX/combined.unique.taxa.list") 
length(combined_taxa)
# 
sum(combined_taxa == "")
# 
sum(combined_taxa != "")
# 

my_taxa_clean <- combined_taxa[combined_taxa != ""]
length(my_taxa_clean)
# 
str(my_taxa_clean)



# # Your cleaned taxa list (can include synonyms, candidatus, or higher ranks)
# my_taxa <- c("Firmicutes",..., "Clostridium")
 
# Output directory structure
CSV_DIR <- "XXXX/results/csv_lineages"
WB_PATH <- "XXXX/results/LPSN_result_Master.xlsx"
LOG_DIR <- "XXXX/results/logs"


# Run API function
# set batch size as needed. Small batches is a bit slower as it opens and saves to excel more often.


process_lpsn_candidatus_batch(
# process_lpsn_cached_batches(
  taxa_list     = my_taxa_clean,
  csv_path      = CSV_DIR,
  workbook_path = WB_PATH,
  log_path      = LOG_DIR,
  user          = Sys.getenv("DSMZ_API_USER"),
  password      = Sys.getenv("DSMZ_API_PASSWORD"),
  batch_size    = 50,    # Processes 50 unique taxa per Excel sheet
  pause_min     = 0.5,   # Minimum delay between API calls (seconds)
  pause_max     = 1.5,   # Maximum delay between API calls (seconds)
  use_timestamp = TRUE   # Appends date/time to the Excel filename
)

# Input: xxxx taxa. Unique/Cleaned: xxxx. Deduplication log saved to 'deduplicated_taxa.txt'.

# Run Complete. Total time: 4.222129 hours

```


## Combine log files
This file lists all the taxa that were not found  - these taxa can be searched for using the LPSN site or other database as suitable.
The placeholder names from various databases end up here as they do not exist in the official lineage


```{r}

# set location of log files to combined and where the output should be

log_dir <- "agrf_0098/LPSN/results/logs"
output_file <- "agrf_0098/LPSN/results/all_missing_taxa.txt"

# List all .txt files in the directory
files <- list.files(path = log_dir, pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

# Read all files into a single list, merge, and save
merged_content <- files |>
  # Read each file as a character vector
  lapply(readLines, warn = FALSE) |>
  # Flatten the list into one long vector
  unlist() |>
  # Optional: Remove any empty strings and duplicates
  unique() |>
  (\(x) x[x != ""])() |>
  # Sort alphabetically
  sort()

# Write the final combined file
writeLines(merged_content, output_file)

message("Merged ", length(files), " files into: ", output_file)

# Merged 47 files into: XXXX/results/all_missing_taxa.txt

```



### Combine all batch results into a single file

```{r}
library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)

# Set input and output files
input_workbook <- "XXXX/results/LPSN_result_Master_20260422_1514.xlsx"
output_csv     <- "XXXX/results/LPSN_Master_Combined.csv"

# Get names of all sheets in the workbook
sheet_names <- openxlsx::getSheetNames(input_workbook)

# Read, convert to character, and combine
combined_data <- sheet_names |>
  lapply(\(s) {
    df <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(input_workbook, sheet = s)
    # Convert every column to character to prevent type mismatch
    df |> dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
  }) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Save to CSV (or use sep = "\t" for TSV)
write.csv(combined_data, output_csv, row.names = FALSE)

message("Successfully combined ", length(sheet_names), " sheets into: ", output_csv)

# Successfully combined 47 sheets into: XXXXX/results/LPSN_Master_Combined_XXXX.csv

```


## Processing automated taxonomy update - lookup

A new table is created that uses the returned LPSN names and maps them to the original taxonomy table containing ASVs. The result is Final_Taxonomy_Matched.csv which contains the ASVs, the original lineage, then a column indicating which term in the lineage was matched in the LPSN database and all upstream levels.

This file allows you to check manually & curate the taxonomic lineage as desired.

```{r}
# load function
source("LPSN_API_functions.R") 

###### usage example
# Define Paths and file names
master_file <- "agrf_0098/LPSN/results/LPSN_Master_Combined.csv"
tax_file    <- "agrf_0098/taxonomy_pre_LPSN.csv"
result_file <- "agrf_0098/LPSN/Final_Taxonomy_Matched.csv"

#Define Custom Ranks/Columns (Optional) ---
# You can provide these in any case (lower, UPPER, Sentence)

# rank order to check
my_check_ranks <- c("species", "genus", "family", "order", "class", "phylum", "kingdom")

# columns from the LPSN master file to add to the taxonomy file
my_append_cols <- c("domain", "kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species")

#Run the Function ---
process_taxonomy_lookup(
  master_path = master_file,
  taxonomy_path = tax_file,
  output_path = result_file,
  check_ranks = my_check_ranks, # Now an input
  append_cols = my_append_cols  # Now an input
)

# Done. Results in: XXXXX/Final_Taxonomy_Matched.csv
```
